title: sp-5.1: the key `human.holds_crayon` (appears) and the recipe `crayon prop moves` (moves) cannot both pass
text: `human.holds_crayon` observes `{kind: prop, actor: crayon, expect: appears}` and reads the crayon ABSENT on f939 (the frame before the story point: `read_prop` refuses an `appears` prop that is in the blocking before it). The recipe `{kind: stage, actor: crayon, expect: moves, by: [1]}` reads the crayon's anchor on f939 and on f1009 and refuses a prop with no anchor on either (`read_stage`: `'crayon' has no anchor at f939 or f1009`). Both read the same actor on the same frame, so a crayon that is absent on f939 fails `moves` and one that is present on f939 fails `appears`. Measured on animatic 09 draft with the crayon `on: 940`: `after human.holds_crayon` passes (`'crayon' appears, 65960 px change within 150 px of (930, 402)`), `measure 'crayon prop moves from clawd to human'` fails with the text above. The staging is the one the story point asks for (Clawd holds the crayon out on 940, it travels 270 px to her hand by 968 on `at` keys, declared contacts crayon-clawd and crayon-human). Either `moves` should read from the first frame the prop is on stage inside the window (as `returns` does with its `went`), or the key should say `present`. Ruled by the director in the screenplay: sp-5.1's recipe now reads the crayon's carrier changing from clawd to human (kind stage, expect carried-by).
before: crayon on 940: `appears` ok, `moves` FAIL; crayon on before 939: `appears` FAIL, `moves` ok
after: one reading of a prop's first frame for both
